title: Australia Skilled Worker Visa 2026: UK Guide
metaDescription: Australia skilled worker visa 2026 for UK applicants: points-tested visas, skills assessment, occupation lists, English requirements and state nomination.
headline: Australia Skilled Worker Visa 2026: A Guide for Applicants in the UK

sections.title: Which skilled visa fits you
sections.content:
Australia's main points-tested skilled visas are the independent subclass 189, the state-nominated subclass 190 and the regional subclass 491. The 189 visa needs no sponsor or nomination, while 190 adds points for state nomination and 491 adds points for regional nomination with a pathway to permanent residence.

Your occupation must be on the relevant skilled occupation list for your visa, and lists differ between visa subclasses. An occupation that qualifies for state nomination may not qualify for independent migration, so checking the list for your exact visa subclass is the first step, not an afterthought.

sections.title: Skills assessment and points
sections.content:
Most applicants need a positive skills assessment from the assessing authority for their occupation before lodging an expression of interest. Assessments check qualifications and, for many trades and professions, work experience against Australian standards, and processing can take months.

Points are awarded for age, English ability, skilled work experience, qualifications, Australian study, partner skills and nomination. The pass mark is only the entry threshold, and invitation rounds often select candidates well above it. Strong English scores are one of the fastest ways to lift a points total.

sections.title: English, health and character checks
sections.content:
English requirements vary by visa and occupation, with higher scores earning more points and some occupations demanding superior English for registration. Accepted tests include IELTS, PTE Academic and other approved tests, and results must be current when you are invited.

Health examinations and police certificates are required for most applicants, and processing times vary with case complexity. Applicants should also budget for the visa charge, skills assessment fees, English testing and document translation, since total costs run well beyond the visa fee alone.

sections.title: Applying from the United Kingdom
sections.content:
UK applicants lodge an expression of interest through SkillSelect, then wait for an invitation before lodging a visa application. State nomination adds a separate application step, and each state sets its own occupation priorities, residency expectations and application windows.

Keep employment references, payslips and qualification documents ready in the format your assessing authority requires. Vague reference letters are a common cause of assessment delays, so references should state job title, duties, dates and hours worked in clear detail.

faqs.q: What is the difference between subclass 189 and 190?
faqs.a: Subclass 189 is an independent points-tested visa with no sponsor or nomination, while subclass 190 requires nomination by an Australian state or territory and awards extra points. State nomination also restricts where you must initially live. Your occupation must be eligible for the subclass you choose.

faqs.q: Do I need a skills assessment for Australia?
faqs.a: Most points-tested skilled visa applicants need a positive skills assessment from the relevant assessing authority before lodging an expression of interest. The authority and evidence required depend on your occupation, and assessments can take months, so start this step early in your planning.

faqs.q: How many points do I need for a skilled visa?
faqs.a: The pass mark is the minimum to lodge an expression of interest, but invitation rounds often select candidates well above it. Points come from age, English, experience, qualifications and nomination. Improving English scores or gaining state nomination are common ways to become competitive.

faqs.q: Can I include my family in my application?
faqs.a: Yes, you can usually include a partner and dependent children in a skilled visa application. Partners may also contribute points if they meet age, English and skills requirements. Health and character checks apply to most adult dependants as well as the main applicant.
